transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-06
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Sequoia Head of Platform), Carlos Mendes (SRE), Priya Singh (FinOps), Omar Ruiz (Eng Manager)
Shared links: deck: https://bit.ly/redwood-sequoia-deck, demo recording will be shared, sample-costs.xlsx (internal)

Auto Summary:
- Quick console walkthrough focusing on per-route usage analytics, cost mapping, and chargeback flows.
- Customer wants to validate chargeback feasibility for multi-team product lines, see low-latency vs cost tradeoffs, and confirm private/VPC constraints.
- Agreed next steps: send pricing scenarios, SOC2 + network brief, schedule pilot ingest for two routes.

Topics covered:
- Route-level telemetry and tags
- Per-route cost breakdown and attribution
- Console reports: percentile latency, cold-starts, KV cache hits
- Pilot scope and success criteria (cost delta, SLA targets, integration effort)

Transcript body:
[00:00:03] Maya: Okay everyone i think we're live. thanks for taking the time. uh quick intro from our side, i'm maya patel, account executive for redwood inference and with me is ethan cho, he's our solutions engineer.
[00:00:12] Ethan: hey all, quick wave. i'll drive the console demo, show the usage lens and route cost map.
[00:00:18] Lena: hi thanks, lena here. priya and carlos are on from our side. we're mostly interested in per-service cost apportionment and how you'd suggest we charge product teams.
[00:00:30] Priya: yeah our finance team wants to see a clean mapping from spikes to dollars, ideally daily and per-route.
[00:00:36] Maya: cool that's exactly what we'll walk through. first slide is a short agenda, then ethan jumps into the console.
[00:00:44] Ethan: ok i'm sharing my screen — can everyone see the console? looks like yes. starting top-level usage dashboard: tokens, requests, and cost bands. the view defaults to last 30 days but we can change window.
[00:01:02] Ethan: one thing to call out — cost here is a computed estimate using your model mix and route weights, it maps per-token unit costs and runtime. so it's not just tokens * price, it factors in batch/latency profile.
[00:01:18] Carlos: sorry to interrupt - when you say model mix do you mean hosted model variants or our own private models?
[00:01:24] Ethan: good q — both. you can pin a route to a hosted model (redwood-hosted) or to a dedicated model pool. the cost calc will use the profile associated with that model - the runtime SLO and average batch size. for private models we ingest your performance profile if you run the benchmark harness.
[00:01:44] [00:01:45] Ethan: moving to the per-route map — i'll filter to 'payments-api' route. you'll see three panes: traffic timeline, cost decomposition, and latency percentiles.
[00:01:56] Ethan: traffic timeline shows requests per minute and average tokens per request. note the spike on Apr 27 around 14:00 — that aligns to the gating release.
[00:02:07] Lena: that spike is the one that blew our last month's forecast — curious how you map that to cost.
[00:02:12] Ethan: yep — cost decomposition shows the token spend (blue), model overhead (orange), and infra/scheduling overhead (grey). it also shows batching efficiency and KV cache hit rate. for that spike the KV cache hit rate dropped to 12% which increased per-token runtime.
[00:02:31] Priya: KV cache hit rate — sometimes i see it called KV cache, sometimes prefix cache in your docs — are those the same?
[00:02:37] Maya: short answer: same concept, different naming in older UI. we've been consolidating the docs. sorry about confusing terms, thanks for flagging.
[00:02:45] Ethan: jumping into the chargeback view: we have an allocation rule engine. you can allocate raw token spend to teams by route tag, or you can apply a blended metric that includes latency premia for SLO-critical routes.
[00:02:59] Ethan: example: payments-api is marked 'SLO-critical', so chargeback shows 15% higher unit than non-critical routes — that's configurable.
[00:03:08] Carlos: can we export by daily buckets? finance needs day-level CSVs.
[00:03:12] Ethan: absolutely, export is built-in. we can also push to S3 or BigQuery on schedule.
[00:03:18] Omar: curious about attribution when multiple services fan-out to a single model endpoint. how do you avoid double-charging?
[00:03:24] Ethan: good point — we attribute tokens and inferred context by upstream route id. if fan-out uses the same endpoint, you can set flow markers so we split proportionally. there's also an option to mark an upstream route as 'shared infra' and remap the cost to a pool.
[00:03:39] [00:03:40] Ethan: switching to the route detail: here's per-request waterfall, includes start-to-end latency, kv cache hit, batch size, model variant, and host pool. see requests marked with 'cold-start' — those have notably higher infra overhead.
[00:03:56] Lena: cold starts are our big pain - any immediate knobs?
[00:03:59] Ethan: two common levers: 1) increase min-resident capacity for that route in dedicated pools, 2) enable prefix/KV warmers for traffic surges. both are toggles in the route config and the console surfaces estimated cost delta live — so you can see the cost vs p99 latency benefit.
[00:04:18] Priya: let's say we enable min-resident and keep same throughput, how do we forecast monthly cost impact?
[00:04:24] Ethan: console 'what-if' simulator — pick policy, apply to route, it shows projected monthly spend, unit cost per 1k requests, and expected latency shift. i'll run a toy: enabling min-resident of 2 GPUs for payments-api shows +22% infra cost but reduces p99 by 45ms.
[00:04:44] [00:04:45] Ethan: switching to tagging: we recommend tags at route creation — product team, environment, business-unit. these tags drive the allocation rules.
[00:04:56] Carlos: do tags get retroactive attribution? we have thousands of historical routes.
[00:05:00] Ethan: yes we can backfill tags via import csv; attribution replays for the selected window. note heavy historical reprocessing can be throttled if you reprocess >30 days.
[00:05:12] Maya: quick note on security — you asked earlier about VPC/private. our private offering runs a customer-managed control plane; all token logging can be disabled and KMS integrated for keying. we'll share the SOC2 + network brief after.
[00:05:25] Lena: do you keep transcripts or request bodies by default? we need to be sure no PII is stored.
[00:05:30] Maya: by default we store request metadata and token counts only; payload retention is off in private mode. audit logs show who queried billing but not request bodies unless you enable it.
[00:05:40] [00:05:44] Ethan: heading into the Optimize tab — suggestions pane pulls runtime telemetry and proposes batching/quantization or model swap recommendations. for an eval we ran on your test route, swapping to a quantized variant reduced cost 35% with a small BLEU-style delta on accuracy for the NLU model.
[00:06:05] Priya: do you provide regression testing hooks? we need to validate quality loss per change.
[00:06:10] Ethan: yes, the optimize module ties into eval sets; you can register prompt sets and it gives quality regressions and alerts if model-swap crosses thresholds.
[00:06:18] [00:06:35] Ethan: now a short live drill — i'm going to create a temporary rule that applies a regional fallback for low-cost zone, route-level. applying now... ok created. watch the cost projection update on the right.
[00:06:47] Carlos: i see the line items, though curious about exchange rates — we bill in USD but our accounting is in EUR.
[00:06:54] Maya: we can export in USD and also provide monthly exchange-rate adjustments; many customers run conversion in BigQuery after export.
[00:07:02] [00:07:05] Ethan: moving forward to anomaly detection — console flags abrupt increases in per-token cost or sudden drop in kv hit rate. you can configure alerting to PagerDuty, Slack, or webhook. here's a sample alert that fired for your test cluster in march.
[00:07:21] Lena: what about shared model pools across regions? does the cost show per-region breakouts?
[00:07:26] Ethan: yes region is a primary dimension. the route map can pivot by region, model, or product tag.
[00:07:33] [00:07:55] Ethan: quick question for you — what's your target SLA for payments?
[00:07:59] Lena: p99 300ms, but p95 is okay at 120ms — it's mostly the p99 tail we want to clamp.
[00:08:06] Ethan: good — we can create an SLO policy and show a canary rollout with automatic fallback to a cheaper model when error or latency crosses threshold.
[00:08:17] Omar: that fallback behavior — does it risk exposing lower-quality outputs to customers?
[00:08:21] Ethan: it's configurable: fallback can be to a model variant labeled 'safe' that enforces guardrails, or you can route to degraded UX with a retry logic. you set the thresholds and the console shows expected quality delta.
[00:08:35] [00:08:40] Ethan: next demo snip: the cost drilldown shows per-token breakdown: compute time, kernel overhead, model charge, and per-request scheduling. these are estimates but we've benchmarked against dedicated pools to be within 7-12% error.
[00:08:58] Carlos: do you ingest our own telemetry (like traces) to correlate request ids?
[00:09:02] Ethan: yes we can ingest trace ids and ship correlation keys so you can click from a request in Redwood console to your tracing view.
[00:09:09] [00:09:35] Ethan: shifting gears — pilot scoping. proposed pilot: 2 product routes (payments-api, chat-assist) for 30 days, integrate tags, backfill 14 days of history, run chargeback exports weekly, and set two SLOs. success criteria: per-request cost deviation <10% vs baseline and p99 improvement for payments-api by 30%.
[00:09:57] Priya: baseline cost dev <10% — is that realistic given different model variants?
[00:10:01] Ethan: pilot will use 'mirror mode' where traffic also goes to current infra but billing is observational; we won't switch live models unless you opt in. that keeps your production cost stable.
[00:10:12] Maya: for timeline — we can kick off data ingest next week once we get access and tags. engineer time estimate ~8-12 hours for initial config, plus 1 SE deep-dive.
[00:10:25] [00:10:35] Lena: what about legal/procurement — we have a standard vendor contract review process.
[00:10:39] Maya: we have standard enterprise terms and can share a redlined starter contract. for private deployments we do a site review and network checklist.
[00:10:50] Ethan: quick demo close — i'll show the CSV export flow: pick time window, pivot by tag, download. also the BigQuery push config.
[00:10:59] [00:11:05] Ethan: last piece — cost optimization suggestions. console lists candidate actions sorted by ROI: quantize model A (35% cost save), enable persistent warmers (10% cost increase but 40ms p99 reduction), reduce max tokens on low-value routes (8% save). each suggestion links to evals and simulated impact.
[00:11:30] Priya: can we automate applying suggestions for low-risk routes?
[00:11:33] Ethan: yes you can set a policy to auto-apply suggestions below a quality delta threshold, and get a report each week.
[00:11:40] [00:12:05] Maya: ok we're nearing the end. recap: we'll send pricing scenarios and sample cost projection, share SOC2 + VPC brief, and schedule pilot kickoff for week of 5/19 pending your approval.
[00:12:18] Lena: thanks. quick ask — can we get a short playbook on chargeback options and examples from other customers?
[00:12:24] Maya: yes we'll include a one-pager with three common allocation patterns: route-tag, blended SL O premium, pooled infra.
[00:12:34] Priya: do you have any references on the accuracy of your cost model compared to raw cloud billing?
[00:12:39] Ethan: we include a methodology doc — we'll send benchmark results; our typical deviation vs cloud-level invoice is 7-12% for GPU-backed workloads.
[00:12:50] [00:13:05] Lena: any gotchas for us to plan for during pilot?
[00:13:08] Maya: two things — tag hygiene: if routes are poorly tagged attribution is messy; second is historic backfill can take time for large windows.
[00:13:18] Omar: on the integration side, what endpoints do we call? is it just a route registration API?
[00:13:22] Ethan: yes a small SDK and a route registration endpoint; we can do it via terraform or REST. i'll send the sample code.
[00:13:32] [00:13:40] Maya: i'll capture action items — Maya to send pricing and playbook, Ethan to share quickstart and sample curl, Priya to confirm top 5 routes, schedule pilot. thanks everyone.
[00:13:50] Lena: thank you all.

(there was a short side discussion about integrating Prometheus metrics at ~00:23 but transcription cut in places; some words like 'K V cache' were transcribed as K V cash in one snippet)

Meeting end: 15:54 PDT

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional mis-words for acronyms, speaker label bleed where multiple speakers overlapped.
